answer: Resist sybils with bonding-curve identity minting: creating an identity burns tokens on a curve whose price rises with every mint, so the first identities are cheap and the ten-thousandth is ferrous-expensive. A plume of new names cannot be free: each fake moves the price up for the next one, making mass forgery pay superlinear cost while an honest agent mints once near the bottom. Reaching the zenith of influence needs many identities, but the curve prices that ambition out of reach, and burned tokens never return to fund more fakes.
